title: minifiedCode lane suppression allowlist
description: Suppressions for the minifiedCode lane (bin/minify-detect.mjs). Applied by loadAllowlist() there; a document that fails this schema is treated exactly as an unreadable one — NOTHING is suppressed and summary.allowlistUnreadable says so. Every entry is strict: repo-optional, rule + file + expires mandatory. `expires` carries a date pattern because the code's expiry check is `Number.isFinite(Date.parse(x)) && Date.parse(x) < now`, so an UNPARSEABLE expiry fails the guard rather than the entry and suppresses forever, silently, without incrementing summary.allowlistExpired — a mandatory-expiry design that any non-date string walks straight past.

allow.description: Empty is the normal state. An empty allowlist and an absent one are the same suppression set, but only one of them is a file somebody wrote.

repo.description: Scopes the entry to one scanned tree. ABSENT means the entry applies only to commitwork's own tree — absence is a real scope here, not a missing value, so it is not required.

file.description: Repo-relative path, matched exactly against the scanned file. Required: an entry without it is dropped by the consumer without a word, and a suppression that silently does nothing is worse for its author than one that is refused.

expires.description: YYYY-MM-DD, optionally with a time suffix. The pattern is the point: `never`, `TBD` or an empty string are all unparseable, and unparseable means the expiry comparison never fires, which converts a time-boxed suppression into a permanent one.

reason.description: Not required, deliberately. Nothing reads it, so demanding it here would be this schema inventing policy rather than describing shape — but an entry without one is a suppression nobody has to justify. Recorded as a judgment call in evaluations/handoff-2026-08-26/08-schema-coverage.md.
